metadata.title: Cybersecurity Control Catalog - Software Supply Chain

props.name: keywords
props.value: IM8, GovTech, Singapore, cybersecurity, Software Supply Chain

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Absence of centralised code repository and version control increases the risk of code inconsistencies, loss of code history, and difficulties in collaboration, potentially leading to errors and security vulnerabilities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Manage the codebase in a central code repository with version control.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Use common internal platforms that provide Git repository services.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Allowing unsigned commits in the code repository introduces the risk of unauthorised or malicious code changes, compromising the integrity and security of the software development process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Configure the code repository to reject unsigned commits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Use GitLab's push rules, GitHub's branch protection rules or similar code repository controls to reject unsigned commits on push.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Without peer review and approval before merging, there is an increased risk of introducing undetected coding errors, security vulnerabilities, and maintaining codebase consistency may become challenging.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Require peer review and approval by a designated reviewer before merging into the default branch.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Use GitLab's protected branch and merge request settings, GitHub's branch protection settings or similar code repository controls to enforce this.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Failure to pin direct and transitive dependency versions in the application's manifest may lead to version drift, introducing compatibility issues, security vulnerabilities, and unpredictability in the software environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Pin direct and transitive dependency versions in the application's dependency manifest.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Dependency manifests such as package-lock.json for npm and Pipfile.lock for pipenv allow you to pin dependency versions.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Inconsistent and unmanaged releases may lead to configuration drift, increased likelihood of errors, and unapproved changes to releases.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use a consistent build and release process that generates a record of how the release artefact was built and deployed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Consider automated build and deploy tools such as CI/CD Pipelines, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and other scripts, which allow for signing and validation of build artefacts. If automation is not possible, develop and implement release management processes.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Failure to install only pinned versions of dependencies during deployment increases the risk of introducing unforeseen changes, compatibility issues, and potential security vulnerabilities into the deployed environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only install pinned versions in the manifest when installing dependencies during deployment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Use package manager commands such as npm ci for npm and pipenv sync for pipenv that ensure only versions specified in the manifest are installed rather than the latest version.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Unsigned code and container images pose a risk of tampering, impersonation, and the injection of malicious code during the build process, compromising the integrity and security of the deployed software.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Sign software artefacts such as code and container images using a trusted source during build.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Use tools or services like Cosign or AWS Signer to sign and verify code.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Without verifying the signatures of code and artefacts before deployment or runtime, there's an increased risk of deploying tampered or malicious software, compromising the integrity and security of the system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Verify the signatures of code and artefacts before deployment or runtime.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Implement a signature verification step such as a pipeline stage or Kubernetes Admission Controller.

props.name: risk-statement
props.value: Restricting code repositories to closed source can result in duplicated efforts, hinder collaborative learning, and lead to missed bugs or vulnerabilities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Share source code internally to enhance code quality, accelerate innovation, and improve problem-solving efficiency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Adopt InnerSource practices for internal collaboration, utilising Git platforms to manage and share code repositories internally. Source code should be evaluated for suitability for InnerSourcing, such as the use of confidential algorithms or embedded sensitive data. The InnerSource guidelines published in the Singapore Government Developer Portal provide a useful framework for code sharing.
